results.title: Türkiye formally adopts new name as part of official country branding strategy
results.content: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has directed all Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), public institutions and media organisations to adopt the name Republic of Türkiye in all official communications, replacing the previously used name, Republic of Turkey.

results.title: Gold Fields says Tarkwa mine has contributed US$3.3bn to Ghana
results.content: Gold Fields Ghana Limited says it has paid US$3.3 billion to the Government of Ghana in royalties, corporate taxes and dividends from its operations at the Tarkwa mine. In a media statement issued on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the company also disclosed that it had invested more than US$5 billion in developing and sustaining the mine. The statement comes as the government reviews the company's application to renew the Tarkwa mining leases. Gold Fields said it submitted the application in November 2025, following a request from the government to do so early. Gold Fields said it was among the mining companies invited to invest in Ghana in the early 1990s as part of efforts to revive the country's gold sector.

results.title: JAY Foundation urges post-discharge care for premature babies and their mothers in Ghana
results.content: For many families, the arrival of a baby is a moment of joy. But when a child is born prematurely, that excitement can quickly give way to fear, uncertainty and emotional distress. Mothers may have to cope with an unexpected delivery, separation from their newborns and the anxiety of watching them receive specialised care in incubators or neonatal intensive care units. The challenges often continue after discharge, with the cost of treatment, repeated hospital visits and the demands of caring for a fragile newborn placing additional pressure on families. For Lamisi, a mother who delivered her baby prematurely at eight months, the experience began with what she expected to be a routine antenatal visit. results.title: COP31: AirQo joins push for more clean air funding to reach Africa’s most affected communities
results.content: Uganda-based air quality network AirQo has called for increased funding to tackle air pollution in Africa, warning that the continent's monitoring capacity remains far behind that of other parts of the world. The organisation says more investment is needed to strengthen air quality monitoring, support local institutions and ensure that funding commitments made at international climate summits translate into action in the countries and communities most affected. results.title: COP31: EPIC joins calls for doubling of clean air funding for Africa, Asia and Latin America
results.content: The University of Chicago’s EPIC Air Quality Fund has called on philanthropic funders to double their annual support for clean air initiatives in Africa, Latin America and parts of Asia to about US$16 million by the next United Nations climate summit. The three regions, excluding China and India, currently receive a combined US$8.3 million annually for philanthropic air quality work, according to Christa Hasenkopf, Director of the Clean Air Program and founder of the EPIC Air Quality Fund. Speaking at a COP31 session on financing clean air in the Global South in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 13, she said the proposed increase was achievable with support from a small number of major donors. “We think it’s totally achievable, totally doable. It could just take one person in this room if you are that person with those funding,” Hasenkopf said.

results.title: The UN Succession: Why Grynspan’s growing momentum matters to Africa
results.content: The contest to choose the next Secretary-General of the United Nations is beginning to reveal something more consequential than the electoral fortunes of individual candidates. It is becoming a test of the international community's commitment to multilateralism, the credibility of its calls for institutional reform and the unwritten understandings that help preserve geographical balance in global leadership. Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan is increasingly at the centre of that conversation. In the eighth informal Security Council straw poll on 5 November, she secured 12 encouraging votes out of 15, improving on her previous showing of 11. Argentina's Rafael Mariano Grossi followed with nine, while Guyana's Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett received eight. results.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: Enterprise Risk Management as a leadership responsibility
results.content: Risk management is not simply a compliance function or the responsibility of a risk department. It is a fundamental leadership responsibility that must influence how the organization plans, invests, operates and pursues growth. Every strategic decision carries some level of risk. Changes in market conditions, financial pressures, technology, regulation, cybersecurity, talent availability and supply chains can affect organizational performance. The CEO must ensure that these risks are identified early, properly assessed and managed through clear ownership and appropriate controls.
